The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 05.12.2023.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 05.12.2023 at about 03.30 p.m., petitioner was walking on the extreme side of the Belathur main road holding her mother hand and mother was walking carefully and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing on moving vehicle, at that time one motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-HQ-6528 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life,
came from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to forced impact petitioner fell down and sustained grevious injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Aaxis Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bangalore,
wherein she was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 07 years and was student.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to participate in any sports and lost his childhood happiness.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsels.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle.

Further, this respondent submits that, the erred vehicle insured with the 2nd respondent,
the insurance company and the policy is in force on the date of alleged accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition.
Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 150, 134(c) and 158(6) of M. V. Act.

Further this respondent submits that, the rider of offending was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident, hence this respondent is not obligated to indemnify the 2nd respondent.
Further this respondent denies the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending vehicle and involvement of the said vehicle in the alleged accident.
Further submitted that insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident.
Both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 05.12.2023 at about 3.30 p.m., accident took on near Belathur Main Road due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HQ- 6528 as a result the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, petitioner's father and natural guardian has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15 and also examined Medical Technician at Manipal Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.16 and Ex.P.17 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

sentences.text: ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place she met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined her father and natural guardian as PW.1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Mahazar,
Ex.P.5 is the Sketch, Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 is the Police Intimation, Ex.P.9 is the Hospital Intimation,

Ex.P.10 is the notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.11 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.12 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P.13 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of petitioner, Ex.P.14 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of father of petitioner and Ex.P.15 is the Medical Bills.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 05.12.2023 at about 03.30 p.m.,
petitioner was walking on the extreme side of the Belathur main road holding her mother hand and mother was walking carefully and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing on moving vehicle, at that time one motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HQ-6528 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, came from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to forced impact petitioner fell down and sustained grevious injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Aaxis Hospital, Bangalore, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Whitefield Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.350/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HQ-6528.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".
13.
The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Whitefield Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 350/2023.
The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.

sentences.text:
During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 11 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of riding by the rider of offending motorcycle.

The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.5 (Spot Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.

The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that,
the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
15.

In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16.

entities.text: Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, admittedly respondents have not disputed the accident and also not challenged the charge- sheet submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle.

In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of rider of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53- HQ-6528.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner's father in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.
18. In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that, immediately after the accident petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient.

The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.12 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Manipal Hospital, Bangalore from 05.12.2023 to 06.12.2023 i.e., for 01 day.
He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.
P.5 the doctor has opined that the injuries are grevious in nature.
19. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

In support of his plea, he has produced 02 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.15 to the tune of Rs.78,729/-.
20.
In this case the petitioner has neither adduced the evidence of doctor nor produced any disability certificate to show that she has become permanently disabled.
PW.2 is only record keeper who has only produced the medical documents and her evidence is formal in nature.

Hence,
petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income or under any other heads.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner as well as medical bills submitted by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- including the medical expenses.

sentences.text: LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HQ-6528 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said rider of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 27.03.2023 to 26.03.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 05.12.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
22. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in this accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.

In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be deposited in the name of minor petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank till she attains the age of majority on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
